about: Townspeople barks: one short line each, said as Brea passes within a few metres, never a conversation. Eight sets. A set is chosen by who is speaking and by 'when'; a line is not repeated until its set is used up. Nobody here is named: the speaker label is the calling.

lines: Morning, Reckoner. Crust's good today.
Third pan's yours and the Matron's.
Better you than me.
Trade's steady. We'll lift it all by noon.
Mind the dyke. I raked that edge.
House kite's up. Somebody wants a count.
Tell the Gauge to keep its hours, will you?
A whole morning, back to brine.
It opened on a low tide. I saw the ring
on the mast. Low.
Ask it what it wants, Reckoner.
We'll rake round it.
My grandmother said they never
look at you. They don't. That's the trouble.
If the third goes, the fourth is next.
They share a wall.
I'm not angry at it. You can't be.
I'm angry at the pan for being here.
Two baskets a trip, forty trips.
Don't make me count again.
Coming through. Heavy.
Store's dry and the tally's straight.
Ask the Matron.
Salt for cord, salt for bronze.
Everything on this island weighs the same.
Reckoner. Nothing from the third today,
they tell me.
If you're buying, buy before the Holds
carts come down.

sets.when: on the black beach, once the Pegs have pegged it (0:10 on)
lines: They came up between the hulls.
Walked round every one. Polite.
There's a peg through my drying rack.
I'm leaving it. I'm not a fool.
Pitch is hot if your hands want blacking.
Straight line, hull to pan. I couldn't
lay a strake that true.
Bronze pins, those. Good ones. If any
should come loose, I'd pay.
Boats are still on the map, I'm told.
Boats move. Lucky us.

sets.when: the warning call: an Instrument within 80 m of the breakwater
lines: Instrument on the dyke! Off the pans!
Lamp on the beach road. Keep clear of it.
Pegs in file, coming up the ramp!
It's wading. Leave the sluice alone.
Bell! Bell! Stand out of its line!
It's past. Back to work, the lot of you.

sets.when: once the Datum Line is on the outer dyke (0:21 on)
lines: That paint wasn't there at breakfast.
It's a hand under my doorstep.
I measured. Twice.
Red on the dyke. My mother saw that
at the old boathouse. Then no boathouse.
Can it be scrubbed? I tried. It can't.
They've drawn where the ground should be.
We're standing in the difference.
Don't touch it. Don't lean on it.
Wait for the Reckoner.

sets.when: after the Plumb is down and Brea wears the Guild Whites
lines: Whites suit you. The hat most of all.
You put it over. I watched from the roof.
So it's down. And the line's still there.
Scout's cut. The house means it, then.
Whatever you do next, do it soon.
Paint like that doesn't come alone.
Reckoner. Thank you. That's all.
Lamps in, shutters to. Mise has the watch.
Calm lamps out on the Glass tonight.
Three of them. Wading.
Leave a light in the window.
They don't mind ours.
Wind's dropping. Reed won't cover
a cat in this.
Kindle your bowl, Reckoner.
Tomorrow's long.
Bell's quiet. I'll take quiet.
